q: 1. The consistency test is performed to find .....
explain: The consistency test (Vicat) finds the water percentage that gives a paste of standard consistency, used for setting time and soundness tests.

q: 2. For normal consistency, the penetration in Vicat apparatus should be between .....
explain: Standard consistency is reached when the plunger stops 5 to 7 mm from the bottom, i.e. penetrates about 33 to 35 mm of the 40 mm mould.

q: 3. The pozzolona portland cement gains the strength .....
options: in the same time as ordinary Portland cement
in less time than ordinary Portland cement
In more time than ordinary Portland cement
explain: Pozzolanic reaction with lime is slow, so pozzolana Portland cement gains strength more slowly than ordinary Portland cement.

q: 4. The compound of Portland cement which reacts immediately with water and also sets first is
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts with water immediately and is the first compound to set.

q: 5. Pick up the compound responsible for early strength of cement from the following .....
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) hydrates quickly and gives the early strength (up to about 7 days). C3A causes flash set but contributes little strength.

q: 6. Soundness test of cement determines
explain: The soundness test checks for excess free lime or magnesia, which can cause delayed expansion and cracking.

q: 7. The ability of cement to maintain a constant volume is called
explain: Soundness is defined as cement's ability to retain a constant volume after setting without expansion.

q: 8. For a 50 kg cement bag water required, is
explain: For a standard 50 kg cement bag, about 22.5 litres of water is typically used based on standard mix proportions.

q: 9. The aggregate is called fine aggregate if it is completely retained on .....
explain: As per the answer key, option a. Note: fine aggregate is usually defined as passing 4.75 mm and retained on 0.15 mm, so the wording in the book is loose.

q: 10. The cement mortar mix generally used for internal plastering is .....
explain: As per the answer key, a 1:5 mix is generally used for internal plastering.

q: 11. Stucco are suitable for .....
explain: Stucco is a plaster finish that can be applied on both stone masonry and brick walls.

q: 12. The purpose of adding pozzolana (surki) to lime is to
explain: Pozzolana reacts with lime to impart hydraulic properties, allowing the mortar to set and harden even under water.

q: 13. The clinker is formed at a temperature of range: 1300 - 1600°C
explain: As per the answer key, this option is marked correct; note the range stated in the question (1300-1600°C) is the actual clinker formation range in cement kilns.

q: 14. The small lumps of cement evolved after burning are named as
explain: Clinkers are the small, hard lumps produced when raw materials are burnt in the cement kiln, later ground into cement.

q: 15. In the manufacturing of cement the nodules form the rotary kiln are called .....
explain: The hard nodules that come out of the rotary kiln are called clinker.

q: 16. The main constituents of Portland cement is
explain: Lime is the principal constituent of Portland cement by weight, derived mainly from limestone.

q: 17. Very strong lime mortar is obtained from
explain: Hydraulic lime provides the highest strength among lime types because it undergoes a chemical set rather than just carbonation.

q: 18. The constituent responsible for setting of hydraulic lime under water is
explain: The presence of soluble silica (found in clay) allows hydraulic lime to form compounds that harden in the absence of air.

q: 19. Lime suitable for making mortar of good strength
explain: Hydraulic lime is the standard choice for load-bearing or high-strength mortar because of its superior binding properties.

q: 20. The calcinations of pure lime results in
explain: Calcination of pure limestone (calcium carbonate) drives off CO2, leaving behind pure calcium oxide, also known as quick lime.

q: 21. The advantage of adding pozzolona to lime is
explain: Pozzolana improves lime mortar by increasing strength, enhancing durability against environmental factors, and reducing volume change.

q: 22. The initial setting of cement is caused by formation of
explain: $C_3A$ is responsible for the flash set and initial hardening phase of the cement paste.

q: 23. A slow setting cement has higher percentage of
explain: Dicalcium Silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly and contributes to long-term strength, whereas C3A causes fast setting.

q: 24. The process of applying cement mortar under pressure through a nozzle is called .....
explain: Spraying cement mortar under pressure through a nozzle is guniting (shotcreting).

q: 25. Slump test facilitates .....
options: controlling of water-cement ratio of concrete during construction
the determination of initial and final setting times of cement
the determination of workability of concrete
explain: As per the answer key, option a. Note: the slump test is normally described as a test of workability (option c), and the key answer is debatable. It does help control water content on site.

q: 26. The concrete mix used for general R.C.C. work is .....
explain: A 1:2:4 (cement : sand : aggregate) mix is generally used for R.C.C.

q: 27. Flash setting of cement means
options: stiffening of cement without strength development
explain: Flash set is the premature stiffening of cement paste due to rapid C3A hydration, often without significant strength gain.

q: 28. Pick up the air entraining agent from the following
explain: Various organic compounds, including Vinsol resins and fatty acids, are used to entrain air in concrete.

q: 29. The commonly used lime in white washing is
explain: Slaked lime (calcium hydroxide), being smooth and workable when mixed with water, is the standard material for whitewashing.

q: 30. The main ingredients of Portland cement are
explain: Lime and silica together form the two principal ingredients that combine to produce the cementing compounds in Portland cement.

q: 31. The compound of Portland cement which contributes to the strength after two to three years is .....
explain: Di-calcium silicate hydrates slowly and keeps adding strength for years.

q: 32. Which constituent of the cement, upon a addition of water, sets and hardness first
explain: Tricalcium Aluminate (C3A) is the first compound to react and set upon contact with water.

q: 33. The initial and final setting times of quick setting cement are
explain: Quick setting cement has an initial setting time of 5 minutes and a final setting time of 30 minutes.

q: 34. If P is the percentage of water required for normal consistency, water to be added for determination of initial setting time is,
explain: For setting time tests, the water content is standardized at 0.85 times the water required for standard consistency.

q: 35. A badly mixed cement concrete results in
explain: Improper mixing leads to air pockets and uneven aggregate distribution known as honeycombing.

q: 36. Strength of cement, with storage
explain: Cement absorbs moisture from the air during storage (pre-hydration), which reduces its bonding strength over time.

q: 37. The most common admixture which is used to accelerate the initial set of concrete is
explain: Calcium chloride is the most widely used accelerator, speeding up the hydration reaction and initial setting of concrete.

q: 38. High alumina cement is produced by fusing together a mixture of .....
options: limestone, gypsum, bauxite, clay and chalk
explain: High alumina cement is made by fusing limestone and bauxite.

q: 39. Gypsum consists of
explain: Gypsum is chemically calcium sulfate dihydrate, composed of CaSO4 combined with water (H2O).

q: 40. The initial setting time of lime -pozzolana is
explain: Lime-pozzolana mixtures typically have a longer initial setting time of about 2 hours.

q: 41. The required number of bricks (size 9" x 4.5" x 2.25") for 1 cubic meter of cement masonry work is
explain: For standard-sized bricks (9 x 4.5 x 2.25 inches), about 560 bricks are required per cubic meter of masonry, accounting for mortar joints.

q: 42. The final setting time of ordinary portland cement should not be more than
explain: As per specification, the final setting time of OPC should not exceed 10 hours.

q: 43. The seven days compressive strength of a good portland cement, as obtained form the compressive test of cement sand mortar should not be less than for tensile test: 20 and 25 kg/cm2 respectively.
explain: A good Portland cement should achieve a 7-day compressive strength of at least about 175 kg/cm2 in the standard mortar test.
